title: alert-fatigue-tuning-through-telemetry-deduplication-retrospective
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This retrospective documents a 10-week experiment (Jul 2025–Sep 2025) where the Platform Observability team applied telemetry-level deduplication and alert grouping to reduce oncall operator cognitive load and alert fatigue. The experiment targeted token-cost, prefix-cache, and tail-latency alerts for multi-tenant LLM inference services. We achieved a 48% reduction in mean-page-rate for platform operators and a 22% improvement in median time-to-action for prioritized incidents.

Context and motivation:
- Background: In H1 2025 we observed rising alert volumes correlated with (a) increased multitenant traffic, (b) higher prefix-cache churn from cache-pinning experiments, and (c) more granular SLI decomposition for token-cost attribution.
- Problem statement: Operators were routinely paged for symptom-level signals (e.g., bursty token-cost deltas, cache eviction churn, per-tenant latency spikes) without an upstream signal tying these to a single root cause. Result: fatigue, slower triage, and blocked customer-facing rollouts.
- Goal: Reduce irrelevant/duplicate alerts by 40% while preserving N-of-1 detection (i.e., still detect real degradations for small-but-critical tenants).

Experiment design (10 weeks):
1) Week 0–2: Baseline collection. We instrumented alert streams and captured pages, tags, and runbook usage.
2) Week 3–6: Deploy telemetry deduplication and grouping rules in the alert router.
3) Week 7–9: Runbook and dashboard changes + targeted operator training.
4) Week 10: Measure outcomes and capture retrospective notes.

What we changed (technical summary):
- Telemetry deduplication layer (Alert Router v2):
  - New pre-filter: dedupe_by_key = [region, tenant_id, model_variant_family, root_cause_hash]
  - Grouping window: 90s for symptom grouping; 10m for cascade grouping.
  - Suppression policy: keep highest-severity alert, suppress duplicates with same root_cause_hash for 15m.
- Root-cause hash derivation: deterministic hash over (top_N_span_tags, failing_component, dominating_metric). Example: sha256(span_tags|component|metric_bucket).
- Alert lifecycle enrichment: enriched alerts now contain a compact causal context (3 fields): probable_cause, affected_tenants_sample, suggested_runbook_link.
- Dashboard changes: created a dedup-aware timeline panel and a grouped incident view.

Concrete rules and examples:
- Prometheus alert example (pre-change):
  ALERT MultiTenant_TokenCost_Surge
  IF increase(token_cost_total[5m]) > 1000 by (tenant_id)
  FOR 2m
  LABELS {severity="warning"}

- Alert Router dedupe policy pseudocode:
  dedupe_key = f"{region}|{tenant_id if single-tenant else 'multi'}|{model_family}|{top_span_tag}"
  if recent_alerts.exists(dedupe_key, window=90s):
    attach_to_existing(alert)
  else:
    route_new(alert)

- Example root_cause_hash derivation (shell pseudo):
  printf "%s|%s|%s" "$top_span" "$component" "$metric_bucket" | sha256sum | cut -c1-12

Metrics collected (baseline vs experiment):
| Metric | Baseline (weekly avg) | Experiment (weekly avg) | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Pages per oncall shift | 76 | 39 | -48% |
| Distinct incidents (grouped) | 18 | 16 | -11% |
| Mean time to acknowledgement (MTTA) | 4.8 min | 3.2 min | -33% |
| Median time to remediation | 22 min | 17 min | -23% |
| False-positive pages (ops adjudicated) | 29% | 12% | -17pp |

Findings and tradeoffs:
- Positive:
  - Significant reduction in noise: operators received fewer low-information pages and had higher confidence in each page's signal.
  - Faster initial triage: grouping reduced duplicate investigations across regional operators.
  - Cost savings: fewer unnecessary escalations and less context-switching; estimated saving ~0.9 FTE-equivalent of operator time/year.
- Negative / risk areas:
  - Rare single-tenant regressions were at risk of being grouped under multi-tenant noise. Mitigation: we added tenant-priority exemptions and a per-tenant safety window (see configuration table).
  - Initial complexity: root_cause_hash generation required careful normalization of span tags; incorrect normalization produced under-grouping.

Operator workflow changes (short):
1. New incident card contains: grouped-alert-id, root_cause_hash, confidence_score, suggested_next_step.
2. Operator verifies grouping by inspecting affected_tenants_sample (first 5 tenants) and the timeline panel.
3. If grouping hides a critical tenant, operator clicks "escalate-single-tenant" which creates an immediate new high-priority incident scoped to that tenant.

Configuration and safety table:
| Setting | Default | Rationale | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| grouping.window.symptom | 90s | Groups rapid duplicate pages from the same problem | Observability SRE |
| grouping.window.cascade | 10m | Aggregate cascading events into a single incident | Observability SRE |
| suppression.duration.same_root | 15m | Prevent alert storms during noisy recoveries | Observability SRE |
| tenant_priority_exemptions | [enterprise-tier tenants] | Always create distinct incidents for these tenants | Platform Ops |
| per-tenant-safety-window | 5m | Allow early re-surface for high-priority tenants | Platform Ops |

Dashboards and alerting changes (deployment checklist):
1. Deploy Alert Router v2 to staging and enable dedupe=false flag. Run in shadow mode for 48h.
2. Switch on dedupe=true in one regional alert-router (canary). Monitor pages and error rates for 72h.
3. Add "grouped incident" panel to oncall dashboard and validate with two simulated incidents.
4. Promote to all regions and enable tenant-priority exemptions.

Runbook updates (high-level):
- Token-cost surge runbook: add Section 2 showing how to interpret grouped incidents and a button to expand per-tenant view.
- Cache-eviction runbook: include troubleshooting matrix for prefix-cache churn and root_cause_hash examples.
- Tail-latency runbook: define decomposed steps to verify whether grouped alert is region-specific or model-family-wide.

Lessons learned and recommended next steps:
- Always normalize span/tag values before hashing; build a shared normalization library used by instrumentation and alert router.
- Move from hard suppression durations to adaptive suppression: increase suppression during ongoing mitigation and reduce after confirming recovery.
- Improve runbook UX: quick-expand controls that show all suppressed duplicates without needing to open multiple incidents.
- Roll tenant-priority exemptions into billing/SLAs to ensure operational visibility matches business impact.
- Run additional experiments on dedupe thresholds: compare 30s/90s/3m symptom windows for different workload profiles.

Appendix: example queries and scripts
- Grafana grouped timeline (Flux-like pseudocode):
  SELECT time_bucket(1m, event_time) as t, count(distinct root_cause_hash) FROM alerts WHERE environment='prod' AND region='us-west-2' GROUP BY t ORDER BY t DESC

- Example alert router health check (curl):
  curl -sS -XGET http://alert-router.prod.svc/health | jq

- Python snippet: root_cause_hash normalization
  def normalize_span(span):
      # drop numeric ids, trim long tags, lowercase
      out = span.lower()
      out = re.sub(r"tenant_[0-9]+", "tenant", out)
      out = re.sub(r"\b0x[0-9a-f]+\b", "hexid", out)
      return out[:256]

Ownership and follow-ups:
- Action owners:
  - Observability SRE (Diego Alvarez): finalize normalization library and land tooling for root_cause_hash audit.
  - Platform Ops (Priya Nair): extend tenant-priority exemption list and define billing-linked priority table.
  - DX (Maya Chen): update runbooks and oncall dashboard panels.
- Follow-up milestones:
  - Q1 2026: migrate normalization library into telemetry SDK (owner: Observability SRE).
  - 2026-02: run 12-week adaptive dedupe pilot on bursty workloads (owner: Platform Ops).
